criteria.criterion: The canonical tag matcher accepts `[non-codebase]` and `[operator-attested]` case-insensitively, rejects the `[operator_attested]` near-miss, and uses a NON-capturing alternation so `findall()` arity is unchanged — proved by a unit test asserting `operator_attested_ac_texts` returns a list of `str`, not tuples.
Every existing test that feeds `[operator-attested]` passes UNCHANGED, demonstrating the alias still works.

`[non-codebase]` and `[operator-attested]` produce identical outcomes across the plan-time lint, the laundering guard, the provenance guard, the AC-checkbox precheck, and the close path — proved by parametrizing those suites over both spellings.
`project.measurement-provenance` fires on a `[non-codebase]`-tagged plan (the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` trigger was widened), proved by a test asserting the trigger matches both spellings.
Author-facing guidance emits `[non-codebase]` only; `[operator-attested]` appears in NO documented surface, enforced by a NEGATIVE test over the packaged guide.
`src/rebar/audit/page.py` renders a legacy `kind: "operator-attested"` verdict identically to a new `kind: "non-codebase"` one, proved by a test over both fixture shapes.

The recognition-side prompts (`completion_verifier.md`, `plan_review_evidence_kind.md`, `plan_review_ac_process_gate.md`, `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md`) instruct that BOTH spellings are recognized, so the LLM classification agrees with the deterministic matcher.

The EMITTED classification vocabulary is cut over in lockstep with the tag, so the deterministic matcher and the LLM's emitted `kind` cannot diverge: the verifier emits `kind: "non-codebase"` (`completion_verifier.md:224`), `contracts.py:116` and `completion_verdict.schema.json` declare it, and BOTH tag-bearing checklist rules in the packaged registry `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` are widened.

`make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and the generated criteria guide is regenerated with its parity check and contract digests updated in the same commit.
